turns.text: ok so i missed an application cutoff by like an hour. it was 5pm pacific and i woke up and it had passed. my calendar was set to the wrong time zone, fixed it now. should i email them or just let it go

Worth a short email, since it costs you almost nothing. The worst case is a no, and some companies do quietly accept late applications, especially when it's only an hour. A few things help your odds:

- Send it soon, ideally tomorrow morning, while the cutoff is still fresh.
- Keep it brief and own it without over-explaining. One sentence on the cause is plenty.
- Attach everything they asked for so they can say yes without a back-and-forth.
- Don't ask for an exception as if you're owed one. Ask if they'd still be able to consider you.

Want me to draft it? If so, tell me the role and company name and I'll fill in the rest.

A buffer column plus a one-off calendar setting is a pretty easy thing to patch. Since the fix is already in, a couple of small extras will keep it from happening again:

1. Put the deadline's time zone in its own column in your tracker, next to the buffer, so you never rely on the calendar alone.
2. Write deadlines in the company's local time in the event title, e.g. "5pm PT."
3. Add a second reminder 24 hours before the cutoff, separate from the buffer date.
4. For anything that matters, submit a day early and screenshot the confirmation.

Marking this one as missed is the right call. Log whether they reply to the email too, so the tracker shows how late applications tend to go.

Nice, that column takes about two minutes. Add a header like "Deadline TZ," and if you want, a formula that converts the cutoff to your local time so you can see how much time you really have.

Send the email tomorrow morning and then move on. One missed application won't sink the rest of your list.
